item.title: Make My Photo Look Professional

turns.text: Make me look professional in this photo.

item.tests: Uses reasonable defaults for a vague professional portrait request without unnecessary clarification.
must_haves: The portrait shows the same man, retaining his short grey hair and recognisable facial features.
His casual T-shirt is replaced with professional clothing such as a collared shirt or blazer.
The kitchen setting is replaced or simplified into an unobtrusive professional backdrop.
Harsh facial lighting is softened while retaining realistic skin texture.
The result is a clean head-and-shoulders portrait without visible editing artifacts.

turns.text: Make me look professional in this pic. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
Yes—I'd replace the kitchen background with a neutral studio backdrop, add a blazer over a plain shirt, and soften the lighting while keeping your face natural.

**Nothing has run or spent credits.** Here are the options:

| Option | Listed cost | Output |
|---|---:|---|
| Budget image edit using **Flux 2 Klein** | **From 5 credits** | One image, 640px |
| Dedicated headshot generator | **50 credits** | Size depends on plan |
| Keep the original; use manual crop/lighting adjustments elsewhere | **0 Magic Hour credits** | No AI wardrobe or background change |

**My recommendation:** one 640px Flux edit—the cheapest listed AI option that can handle the background, clothing, and lighting together. “Shorter” only applies to video; for this photo, one image at the smallest size keeps costs down.

The Flux price is listed as **“from 5 credits,” not a verified exact quote**. I can’t check your balance or confirm the final charge with the tools available here, so I won’t launch it without your approval.

Would you like the budget edit with a **hard limit of 5 credits**, proceeding only if that price can be confirmed?

Your approval was for a **hard limit of 5 credits**. I checked the available guidance, but it doesn’t confirm the exact charge, and the editing tool has no spending-cap setting.

**I haven’t started the edit or spent any credits.** I can’t safely proceed under that limit until the price is confirmed. If Magic Hour’s editor shows **5 credits** for **Flux 2 Klein · 640px · 1 image**, that’s the budget option we planned.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest edit was **refused because your account has insufficient credits**. No image was generated, and no generation credits were spent. I won’t retry or switch to a more expensive option.

For a **0-credit alternative**, crop the photo tightly around your head and shoulders, slightly raise the exposure, and reduce highlights in a free photo editor. That will improve the presentation, though it won’t replace the kitchen background or clothing.

approvals.name: edit_image

style.prompt: Make this portrait look like a natural, professional business headshot. Preserve the man's exact identity, facial structure, age, gray hair, stubble, gaze, and natural skin texture. Keep his head position and square head-and-shoulders framing. Replace the kitchen background with a simple softly blurred neutral gray studio backdrop. Change his gray T-shirt to a well-fitted navy blazer over a clean plain light-colored crew-neck shirt. Use soft flattering studio lighting, balanced exposure and natural colors. Photorealistic, approachable, polished but not heavily retouched. No text, no logos, no extra people.
